A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Text extraction and visual inspection covered all 17 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix B report original Swiss Roll mapping experiments, baseline comparisons, data-quantity ablations, and weather-prediction likelihood results.

after.justification: The original empirical studies are retained and expanded. Appendix A additionally reports neural-parameterization experiments on Swiss Roll and colored MNIST.

M1.justification: The light Gaussian-mixture solver is retained after parameter renaming. However, Appendix A adds a fully neural cost-and-potential variant with model-sampled gradient estimation and Langevin sampling, presented as Algorithm 1. This substantially extends the proposed training and sampling procedures beyond the original tractable mixture implementation.

E1.justification: Swiss Roll mapping and January-to-June weather prediction remain. Appendix A.3 adds colored-MNIST image translation from digit 2 to digit 3 with a prescribed 120-degree hue shift, extending evaluation to a distinct image-generation domain with 3×32×32-dimensional inputs and outputs.

E2.justification: Swiss Roll comparisons add CNF (SS), CGMM (SS), GNOT, DCPEME, parOT, and OTCS alongside the four original baselines, including in the 16K-data experiment. Weather comparisons also expand beyond the retained paired Gaussian-mixture baseline to additional generative, regression, and semi-supervised methods in v2 Table 2.

E3.justification: Weather evaluation adds conditional Fréchet distance, calculated separately for each test input and then averaged, alongside likelihood. New image experiments use 10 versus 200 training pairs. The existing Swiss Roll sample sizes and training budgets, and the weather test-split description, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original source-versus-target unpaired-data ablation is retained as v2 Figure 6. The revision expands the 16K-data sanity check and adds limited analyses of neural versus Gaussian parameterization stability and neural-model behavior with different paired-data quantities in Appendix A.

E5.justification: Both versions report weather results using ± values without specifying their statistical meaning, run counts, or seeds. The new weather table follows the same reporting practice; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive baseline findings, neural-model demonstrations, and weather metric results. The original weather likelihood grid is unchanged: v1 Table 2 becomes v2 Table 1. New Table 2 reports CFD 7.21±0.04 for the proposed method and 7.17±0.07 for CGMM (SS), so the proposed method does not have the lowest reported CFD.

T1.justification: V2 adds the universal-approximation statement in Theorem 3.3, supporting definitions, assumptions, lemmas, and proofs in Appendix D.4, plus the neural-gradient proposition and derivation. It also corrects the log-normalizer sign in v1 Equation 12 through v2 Equation 14, bringing it into agreement with the original empirical training objective.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add universal approximation and arbitrarily accurate recovery as a fourth central contribution. The introduction also adds a broader claim that competing heuristic objectives fail even on simple two-dimensional conditional-distribution problems. The original likelihood, inverse-OT equivalence, and lightweight-solver claims remain.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes comparator failures to deterministic mappings, biased marginal-likelihood estimation, and overfitting, and questions their general applicability. Appendix A adds substantive qualifications about neural-model instability and unresolved scalability. The new blanket weather sample-quality claim is also stronger than Table 2 supports, given CGMM (SS)'s lower reported CFD.

D1.justification: V2 adds focused implementation information for the neural experiments, including MLP widths, activations, learning rates, and U-Net architecture, plus baseline implementation provenance and repository references. Existing Gaussian-solver hyperparameters, GPU/runtime information, and the description of the authors' code as supplementary and planned for public release remain.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands positioning against GAN-based, image-specific, and OT-guided semi-supervised approaches, and explicitly presents the framework as a generalized forward OT solver. New references include Theodoropoulos and Oza, alongside substantial approximation-theory, MCMC, and energy-based-model literature supporting the new contributions.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the original prose remain. Changes include local paragraph rewrites, renamed parameters, expanded loss explanations, and appendix reorganization: original proofs move from A to D, while experimental material is divided between B and C. Much of the expansion is new scientific content rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Swiss Roll figures are substantially expanded and rearranged, while neural-model plots, an image grid, an algorithm box, and a weather comparison table are added. Existing weather and data-usage tables are redesigned and relocated.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, neural/image demonstrations, and correction of the likelihood formula add value. However, major new contributions contain unresolved inconsistencies: Algorithm 1 omits the generated-sample cost term required by Proposition A.1, and Assumption D.7 requires a globally positive density lower bound on R^D, incompatible with probability normalization as written. These problems weaken the added methodological and theoretical claims, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
